text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Chancellor Viktor Klima supports his Social Democrat chief whip Peter Kostelka's plan to pay Bosnian refugees a premium to return to their home country. Meanwhile, he has heavily criticised Carinthia's Freedom Party's directive only to give public construction orders to companies which do not employ foreigners as "economic nonsense".
- Benetton plans to move the workforce at its skimaker Kaestle to sports goods producer Head. However, the agreement for the takeover has yet to be signed.
- Domestic sales of Austrian milk have risen since the country joined the European Union.
- Economic research institute Wifo says privatisations should be done through private companies as this would raise profits for the state.
- Vienna's education council plans to let parents and students give marks on the work of new teachers.
- Austria's government plans to complete negotiations on next year's budget earlier than before.
- Karl-Heinz Grasser, Carinthia's far-right vice state leader has withdrawn his anti-foreigner directive after a barrage of criticism.
- Austria's federal railway OeBB plans to extend its haulage business.
- Die Erste savings bank is expected to present its new chief executive Andreas Treichl and the takeover of the majority in GiroCredit on March 19.
- Telecommunications company Kapsch has taken over Switzerland's Indelco.
- The Chamber of Economy sees Austria weakened by the planned telecommunications law as it says it lacks competitive market regulations.
- Klima seeks a common line with Switzerland for Austria's transit problem.
- About 500 Italian companies are planning to move to Austria due to high taxes and heavy bureaucracy in Italy.
- The European Court of Justice will decide whether to abolish Austria's anonymous savings accounts within the next two years.
